study_identification.author_journal_year: Jalbrzikowski et al., American Journal of Psychiatry, 2019
study_identification.title: Age-Associated Deviations of Amygdala Functional Connectivity in Youths With Psychosis Spectrum Disorders: Relevance to Psychotic Symptoms

study_characteristics.study_objective: Construct normative growth charts of amygdala functional connectivity in typically developing youths, quantify age-associated deviations in youths with psychosis spectrum disorders, and examine associations with psychotic symptoms.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Pearson correlations between deviation scores and positive symptom severity in PSD (r=0.19; q=0.05); group-wise developmental trajectory comparisons across connectivity pairs with multiple-comparison correction (cluster-level).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Youths with psychosis spectrum disorders lack normative age-related decreases in centromedial amygdala connectivity with prefrontal cortex, striatum, thalamus, and occipital cortex; greater deviation from normative CM amygdala–thalamus development relates to more severe positive symptoms.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Normative trajectories show significant age-related decreases in centromedial amygdala connectivity across multiple regions. PSD youths fail to exhibit these decreases between CM amygdala and prefrontal cortices, striatum, occipital cortex, and thalamus (all q<0.1). Age-associated deviations in CM amygdala–striatum and CM amygdala–occipital connectivity are specific to PSD. Greater deviation in CM amygdala–thalamus connectivity is associated with increased positive symptoms (r=0.19; q=0.05).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional data for the psychosis spectrum group precludes within-person developmental inference; adolescent changes can be nonlinear and better captured with longitudinal designs; psychotic symptoms are dynamic and time-varying analyses may be needed.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Growth-chart style normative modeling of seed-based amygdala connectivity provides individualized deviation metrics linked to symptom severity; site/protocol effects addressed via fixed covariates and residual checks; robust motion control via ICA-AROMA and scrubbing.

general_notes.general_notes: Four cohorts (Luna 1, Luna 2, PNC, Pitt FEP) contributed to a combined age range of 10–25 years. AFNI 3dLME included subject random effects to accommodate the longitudinal cohort; age functional forms (linear/inverse/quadratic) assessed. Juelich amygdala ROIs used; analyses masked to GM with AFNI 3dClustSim correction.
